Kiez values are an area-based aggregate derived from the polling districts, not an official original value. Postal votes are officially included in the Bezirk and Berlin totals; at Kiez level, a group's postal votes are distributed proportionally by eligible voters across its polling districts: an estimate, not an official breakdown.

wahl_portal_chapter_karte_subtext: In the winner tab, the coloring shows the leading party per area; in the party tabs, the share of the selected party. Year and level apply only to this chapter.

wahl_portal_chapter_trends_subtext: The map shows the direction and strength of each party's vote-share trend, or the volatility of all parties combined. The toggle and party chips only change the coloring, not the data fetched.
wahl_portal_chapter_uebergaenge_subtext: Each column stands for an election year; each band groups areas with the same party sequence between two elections, even without a change of leading party. Hover or focus shows the exact numbers.
wahl_portal_chapter_extreme_subtext: The maps show, per party, the area with the highest and the lowest vote share in the selected year.
wahl_portal_chapter_methodik_subtext: This lists the sources and licenses of all election datasets, with links to the full methodology page and the license overview.

home_hero_lead: Enter an address. See how loud it is, how hot it gets in summer, how close the nearest S-Bahn station is. Combined into a Kiez score across five dimensions.
home_hook_lead: Enter an address. Combine the data.
home_hook_body: Noise level per street. Heat class per Kiez. Public transport density per Bezirk. Values from the Senate's open data. Compare addresses and Kieze directly. For the flat hunt, the move, the research, or the next argument at the kitchen table.

home_steps_1_text: Enter a Berlin address or click a Kiez on the map.
home_steps_2_text: A Kiez score from 0 to 100 across five dimensions. Culture and crime are added as context.
home_steps_3_text: Switch individual data layers onto the map and compare addresses, Kieze and Bezirke directly.
home_quick_links_lead: One click opens the map at that point, with all data layers next to it.
home_quick_link_pariser_platz_descriptio: Tourist magnet by the Brandenburg Gate. How the data describes a place everyone has stood at once.
home_quick_link_goerlitzer_park_descript: Kreuzberg park, a permanent fixture in the city debate. Noise, green space and social conditions in one spot.
home_quick_link_tempelhofer_feld_descrip: Decommissioned airport, now Berlin's largest open space. Cooler than its surroundings, visible in the climate atlas.
home_quick_link_hermannplatz_description: Junction between Kreuzberg and Neukölln, where the U7 crosses the U8. How a dense inner-city crossing looks in the data.
home_quick_link_frohnau_description: Villa district in northern Reinickendorf, where Brandenburg begins right behind the station. How much Berlin changes toward the north.
home_layer_teasers_lead: Seven shown here in short, including the new context layers culture and crime. Each layer has its own detail page with methodology, licence and last-updated date.
home_layer_teaser_laerm_2023_summary: Strategic noise mapping for Berlin. Ordinal categories per planning area instead of dB point values.
home_layer_teaser_gruenversorgung_2023_s: Green space near housing per person, classified per planning area. Senate Department for Urban Development.
home_layer_teaser_klima_pet_2022_summary: Perceived midday temperature on summer heat days from the Berlin climate atlas.
home_layer_teaser_kiez_score_mobilitaet_: Bus, tram, U-Bahn, S-Bahn and cycling infrastructure combined into the mobility dimension of the Kiez score.
home_layer_teaser_wohnlagen_2024_summary: Housing-location class from the Berlin rent index procedure (simple / medium / good), block-accurate.
home_layer_teaser_kiez_score_kultur_summ: Access to libraries, theatres, museums, cinemas and more. A standalone dimension, not part of the overall score.
home_layer_teaser_kiez_score_kriminalita: Police frequency rate per Bezirksregion. Context, not a safety judgement, not part of the overall score.
home_top_kieze_heading: Every Kiez, one Kiez score across five dimensions
home_top_kieze_footnote: Five equally weighted dimensions make up the overall score (0-100). Culture and recorded crime are added as standalone context but don't feed into the score. Describes distribution, not a rating of individual addresses or people.
home_featured_bezirke_lead: Per Bezirk: profile, Kiez score and answers to the most common questions. Four entry points here, all twelve reachable via search.
home_featured_bezirk_mitte_teaser: Government district, Alexanderplatz, Wedding. The widest range between high politics and the tenement block.
home_featured_bezirk_friedrichshain_kreu: The city's densest population. Noisy, young, in flux.
home_featured_bezirk_pankow_teaser: From Prenzlauer Berg to Buch and Französisch Buchholz. Neighbourhoods with very different conditions.
home_featured_bezirk_neukoelln_teaser: From Reuterkiez to Rudow. The stage for almost every Berlin debate on housing and urban development.

layer_explain_bezirke_short: Administrative Bezirk of Berlin (12 in total)
layer_explain_bezirke_long: Political and administrative division of Berlin into 12 Bezirke. Each Bezirk has its own Bezirk office (Bezirksamt), Bezirk mayor and its own school, sports and health offices. Source: ODIS Berlin (dl-de/zero).
layer_explain_ortsteile_long: Berlin is divided into 96 localities (Ortsteile), historically often independent municipalities. Used for statistics, address assignment and identification (e.g. “I live in Friedrichshain”). Source: ODIS Berlin.
layer_explain_plz_long: Berlin postcode areas. One postcode can cover several Kieze or localities, so it does not match Bezirk or locality boundaries. Source: ODIS Berlin.
layer_explain_bodenrichtwerte_short: Average land price per square metre (as of 2026)
layer_explain_bodenrichtwerte_long: Location values for undeveloped land, set annually by the Berlin Committee of Valuation Experts (Gutachterausschuss). An indicator of land value, not a market price and not a rent. Differentiated by type of use (residential, commercial, mixed-use area).
layer_explain_bodenrichtwerte_scale: Higher = more expensive (inner-city locations often >5,000 €/m², outskirts <500 €/m²)
layer_explain_wohnlagen_2024_short: Residential area rating in the Berlin rent index 2024 (aggregate per planning area)
layer_explain_wohnlagen_2024_long: Aggregated residential area classification from the Berlin rent index (Mietspiegel) 2024 per planning area. For concrete €/m², see the official rent index calculator. The classification is based on location, transport links, local amenities and residential surroundings.
layer_explain_wohnlagen_2024_scale: 1 simple, 2 medium, 3 good, 4 very good, 5 prime location (rent index definition)
layer_explain_milieuschutz_erhaltungsmie: Area with a social preservation order. Protects against displacement through modernisation, conversion into owner-occupied flats and luxury refurbishment. Rent increases and conversions require approval from the Bezirk.
layer_explain_milieuschutz_staedtebau_sh: Urban preservation order (protection of townscape under §172 BauGB)
layer_explain_milieuschutz_staedtebau_lo: Area with an urban preservation order protecting the townscape. Demolition or alterations require approval, often in old-building or Gründerzeit neighbourhoods.
layer_explain_mss_gesamtindex_2025_short: Structural social situation per planning area (MSS 2025, SenStadt Berlin)
layer_explain_mss_gesamtindex_2025_long: Monitoring Social Urban Development 2025: aggregated overall index from status and dynamics indicators per LOR planning area (around 7,500 residents). A structural aggregate, not an assessment of individual addresses or people. Source: Senate Department for Urban Development Berlin.
layer_explain_mss_gesamtindex_2025_scale: Status high / medium / low / very low combined with dynamics positive / stable / negative. Low status does not mean “bad Kiez”, but reflects structural differences in income, employment and education.
layer_explain_laerm_2023_short: Noise pollution in the area (Environmental Atlas 2023)
layer_explain_laerm_2023_long: Categorised overall noise pollution per planning area from the Berlin Environmental Atlas (Umweltatlas) 2023. Covers road, rail and aircraft noise. An indicator of lost residential quiet.
layer_explain_luft_2023_short: Air pollution in the area (Environmental Atlas 2023)
layer_explain_luft_2023_long: Categorised air quality per planning area: nitrogen oxides and particulate matter. Data basis: Berlin Environmental Atlas (Umweltatlas) 2023, traffic model plus monitoring stations.
layer_explain_gruenversorgung_2023_short: Green space provision in the area (Environmental Atlas 2023)
layer_explain_gruenversorgung_2023_long: Per-capita provision of usable public green space in the planning area. An indicator of recreational space and climate resilience. Three categories: low, medium, high.
layer_explain_gruenversorgung_2023_scale: low = little green space, high = well provided
layer_explain_bioklima_2023_long: Bioclimatic stress on hot days per planning area: urban heat island effect, soil sealing, cooling by green space. Relevant for heat protection, especially for older people and the chronically ill.
layer_explain_umweltgerechtigkeit_2023_s: Environmental justice overall: multiple burdens in the area
layer_explain_umweltgerechtigkeit_2023_l: Combined indicator of noise, air, bioclimate and green space provision together with social status. Identifies multiple burdens in disadvantaged areas (Berlin Environmental Justice Report 2023).
layer_explain_umweltgerechtigkeit_2023_s: no high burden to fivefold burden
layer_explain_klima_pet_2022_short: Perceived temperature on hot days at 2 pm (Climate Analysis 2022)
layer_explain_klima_pet_2022_long: Physiological Equivalent Temperature (PET) as a measure of perceived heat stress on a summer day at 2 pm. Takes air temperature, radiation, wind and humidity into account. The map covers built-up areas, street space and green spaces. Water bodies such as lakes and canals have no PET value and stay empty. Source: Berlin Climate Analysis 2022.
layer_explain_klima_pet_2022_scale: below 32 °C neutral, 32 to 41 °C warm to hot, above 41 °C extremely hot
layer_explain_klima_kaltlufteinwirkberei: Area cooled at night by cold air from the surrounding countryside
Urban areas that benefit at night from cold air produced by forests, meadows and parks. Important for night-time cooling in summer and urban climate resilience. Source: Berlin Climate Analysis 2022.
layer_explain_klima_leitbahnkorridor_202: Corridor through which cold air flows into the city at night

Valley structures, street corridors or open spaces through which cold air flows from the surrounding countryside into the city at night. Buildings in these corridors slow down the cooling. Source: Berlin Climate Analysis 2022.
layer_explain_stolpersteine_short: Memorial stone for victims of National Socialism
layer_explain_stolpersteine_long: Brass plaques laid in front of the last freely chosen homes, preserving the names and fates of victims of the Nazi regime. Concept by Gunter Demnig. Data from OpenStreetMap, curated by local Stolpersteine initiatives.
layer_explain_denkmal_2024_short: Listed building or garden monument in Berlin
layer_explain_denkmal_2024_long: Objects from the Berlin list of monuments (Landesdenkmalamt). Includes architectural monuments, garden monuments, archaeological monuments and heritage areas. Data basis for the heritage density aggregate per Bezirk/Kiez.
layer_explain_trinkbrunnen_short: Public drinking fountain (active May to October)
layer_explain_trinkbrunnen_long: Public drinking fountain operated by Berliner Wasserbetriebe. Active seasonally: May to October due to frost protection. Location data from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0).
layer_explain_kuehle_orte_short: Places to cool down in the heat near you
layer_explain_kuehle_orte_long: Places in Berlin that offer relief from the heat: cinemas, libraries, malls, indoor pools, museums and more. Geometry and base tags from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0), supplemented with editorial navigator.berlin enrichment: cool score, air conditioning, summer availability. An offer, not a replacement for public authorities, and no legal entitlement to access.
layer_explain_kitas_2024_long: Recognised Berlin daycare facility 2024. Run by public, church or independent providers. Source: Senate Department for Education, Youth and Families.
layer_explain_schulen_2024_long: Primary school, secondary school, community school or Gymnasium in the Berlin school directory 2024. Source: Senate Department for Education.
layer_explain_einschulbereiche_2024_shor: School catchment area: primary school for children in this area
layer_explain_einschulbereiche_2024_long: Spatially defined primary school district. As a rule, children are assigned to the school of the catchment area they live in. Exceptions are possible. Source: Senate Department for Education, as of 2024.
layer_explain_krankenhaeuser_plan_short: Hospital in the Berlin hospital plan
layer_explain_krankenhaeuser_plan_long: Hospital listed in the Berlin hospital plan (Krankenhausplan) with a statutory care mandate. Source: Senate Department for Higher Education and Research, Health and Long-Term Care.
layer_explain_krankenhaeuser_weitere_sho: Other hospital outside the hospital plan
layer_explain_krankenhaeuser_weitere_lon: Private or specialised hospital outside the Berlin hospital plan, often a private clinic or rehabilitation facility. Source: Senate Department for Higher Education and Research, Health and Long-Term Care.
layer_explain_sportanlagen_2024_short: Sports facility for public or club use
layer_explain_sportanlagen_2024_long: Sports venue (sports ground, sports hall, swimming pool, tennis court) in the Bezirk register of sports facilities 2024. Source: Senate Department for the Interior and Sport.
layer_explain_gruenanlagen_short: Public green space (park, ornamental square, urban forest)
layer_explain_gruenanlagen_long: Officially designated green space for local recreation: park, ornamental square, town square, playground or urban forest. Maintained by the Bezirke's parks departments (Grünflächenämter).
layer_explain_spielplaetze_long: Publicly accessible children's playground with play equipment, maintained by the Bezirk parks department (Grünflächenamt). Source: Berlin green spaces register (Grünanlagen-Register).
layer_explain_nahversorgung_lebensmittel: Local grocery shopping (supermarket, discounter, Späti, bakery)

Shops for daily groceries: supermarket, discounter, convenience store/Späti and bakery. Feeds into the Local amenities dimension of the Kiez score as a density term. Location data from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0).
layer_explain_nahversorgung_apotheke_lon: Public pharmacy for medicines and basic health-related supplies. Part of the local shopping term in the Local amenities dimension. Location data from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0).
layer_explain_nahversorgung_post_long: Post office, parcel shop or postal service point for sending letters and parcels. Part of the local shopping term in the Local amenities dimension. Location data from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0).
layer_explain_schwimmbaeder_short: Public swimming pool or indoor pool
layer_explain_schwimmbaeder_long: Berliner Bäder-Betriebe (BBB) and comparable facilities: indoor pool, outdoor summer pool, combined pool or lakeside bathing beach. Note seasonal opening hours.
layer_explain_kultur_museum_long: Museum or exhibition venue. Part of the culture score (access to cultural venues nearby). Location data from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0).
layer_explain_kultur_galerie_long: Art gallery or exhibition space. Part of the culture score. Location data from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0).
layer_explain_kultur_kunst_im_raum_long: Artwork in public space: sculpture, mural, installation, memorial art. Part of the culture score. Location data from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0).
layer_explain_kultur_theater_long: Theatre, stage or opera house. Part of the culture score. Location data from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0).
layer_explain_kultur_bibliothek_long: Public, academic or special library. Part of the culture score. Location data from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0).
layer_explain_kultur_kino_long: Cinema or picture house. Part of the culture score. Location data from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0).
layer_explain_kultur_soziokultur_long: Cultural centre, community culture centre or arts centre. Part of the culture score. Location data from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0).
layer_explain_kultur_club_long: Club, discotheque or live music venue. Part of the culture score. Location data from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0).
layer_explain_radverkehrsnetz_2025_long: Berlin cycling network including cycling priority routes 2025. Main routes for everyday cycling, developed under the Berlin Mobility Act (Mobilitätsgesetz). Source: SenMVKU.
layer_explain_fahrradstrassen_2024_long: Street designated for cycling (sign 244.1 of the StVO, German road traffic regulations). Other vehicles may only use it by exception and at walking pace. As of 2024.
layer_explain_ubahn_stationen_long: BVG U-Bahn station. 9 lines, around 175 stations in the network. Source: BVG / VBB GTFS.
layer_explain_sbahn_stationen_long: S-Bahn Berlin station. 16 lines, around 170 stations in Berlin and the surrounding area. Source: VBB GTFS / Deutsche Bahn.
layer_explain_tram_haltestellen_long: BVG tram stop, mainly in the eastern part of the city. 22 lines. Source: BVG GTFS.
layer_explain_bus_haltestellen_long: BVG bus stop, city and regional buses. Over 7,000 stops in Berlin. Source: BVG GTFS.
layer_explain_ubahn_netz_long: BVG U-Bahn line routes, 9 lines (U1 to U9). Source: BVG geodata.
layer_explain_tram_netz_long: BVG tram line routes, mainly in the eastern part of Berlin, 22 lines. Source: BVG geodata.
layer_explain_sbahn_netz_short: Berlin S-Bahn line network (operator: S-Bahn Berlin GmbH)
layer_explain_sbahn_netz_long: Routes of the Berlin S-Bahn network, operated by S-Bahn Berlin GmbH (a subsidiary of the DB group). 16 lines, around 330 km of track, the busiest transport axes in Berlin and the surrounding area. Source: OpenStreetMap route relations (ODbL 1.0).
layer_explain_kiez_score_gesamt_short: Environment & infrastructure score overall per planning area (0–100)
layer_explain_kiez_score_gesamt_long: Unweighted mean of the five dimensions (Quiet & air, Green & heat, Mobility, Local amenities, Tenant protection) per LOR planning area. Only measures variables where it is clear which direction is better.
layer_explain_kiez_score_gesamt_scale: Higher = better across all five dimensions
layer_explain_kiez_score_ruhe_luft_short: “Quiet & air” aggregate per planning area (0–100, Kiez score)
layer_explain_kiez_score_ruhe_luft_long: Weighted aggregation of noise and air pollution per LOR planning area. Scale: low = more polluted, high = quieter and cleaner.
layer_explain_kiez_score_gruen_hitze_sho: “Green & heat” aggregate per planning area (0–100, Kiez score)
layer_explain_kiez_score_gruen_hitze_lon: Green space provision and proximity to green spaces plus thermal resilience (bioclimate, PET heat stress, cold air influence zone, cold air flow corridor) per planning area, weighted to 0–100.
layer_explain_kiez_score_gruen_hitze_sca: Higher = more usable green space and better heat protection
layer_explain_kiez_score_mobilitaet_shor: “Mobility” aggregate per planning area (0–100, Kiez score)
layer_explain_kiez_score_mobilitaet_long: Based on the distance from the planning area centroid to the nearest U-Bahn, S-Bahn, tram and bus stop, plus cycling network presence. For each address, the exact address distance overrides the value.
layer_explain_kiez_score_versorgung_shor: “Local amenities” aggregate per planning area (0–100, Kiez score)
layer_explain_kiez_score_versorgung_long: Density of daycare centres, schools, hospitals in the Berlin hospital plan and playgrounds within range of the planning area centroid, plus local shops (groceries, pharmacy, post). Individual radius per POI (daycare 500 m, primary school 600 m, secondary school 1,200 m, hospital 2,000 m, playground 400 m).
layer_explain_kiez_score_versorgung_scal: Higher = better provision of family and health infrastructure
layer_explain_kiez_score_wohnschutz_shor: “Tenant protection” aggregate per planning area (0–100, Kiez score)
layer_explain_kiez_score_wohnschutz_long: Protection against displacement: share of the area inside a Milieuschutz area (residential or urban preservation statute) per planning area. Unambiguously positive: protection in place = better for residents.
layer_explain_kiez_score_kultur_short: “Culture” aggregate per planning area (0–100, Kiez score)
layer_explain_kiez_score_kultur_long: Cultural access: log-damped density of libraries, theatres, museums, cinemas, galleries, community culture centres, public art and clubs nearby (OSM/ODbL). A separate dimension, NOT part of the overall score: culture clusters in the city centre, so it does not drive the headline score.
layer_explain_kiez_score_kultur_scale: Higher = more cultural venues within reach
layer_explain_kiez_score_kriminalitaet_l: Frequency rate of selected housing-relevant offences, 3-year average from the Berlin crime atlas (Kriminalitätsatlas Berlin, Polizei Berlin, dl-de-by-2.0). Granularity Bezirksregion, mirrored onto planning areas. A structural aggregate, NOT part of the overall score. Relates cases only to registered residents, not to tourists/commuters.
layer_explain_kiez_score_kriminalitaet_s: Higher = more recorded cases per resident, not a measure of personal risk and not a judgement of a “good” or “bad” Kiez.
layer_explain_einwohner_dichte_2024_shor: Population density per LOR planning area (residents/km², 31 Dec 2024)
layer_explain_einwohner_dichte_2024_long: Residents per square kilometre per LOR planning area. Neutral demographic context, no judgement: dense is not better or worse than sparse. Source: Statistics Office Berlin-Brandenburg (Amt für Statistik Berlin-Brandenburg) (CC BY 4.0).
layer_explain_einwohner_dichte_2024_scal: Higher = more densely populated, no quality judgement
layer_explain_lor_prognoseraum_short: LOR forecast area (Prognoseraum, Senate Department division)
layer_explain_lor_prognoseraum_long: Life-world-oriented area (Lebensweltlich orientierter Raum), Prognoseraum level. Coarsest of the three LOR levels, used for population forecasts.
layer_explain_lor_bezirksregion_long: Life-world-oriented area (Lebensweltlich orientierter Raum), Bezirksregion level. Middle level of the LOR division, often used as the “Kiez level”.
layer_explain_lor_planungsraum_long: Life-world-oriented area (Lebensweltlich orientierter Raum), planning area level. Finest of the three LOR levels, basis for social-spatial statistics.
layer_explain_wahlbezirke_btw17_long: Geometry of Berlin's polling districts for the Bundestag election 2017. Basis for spatially assigning election results at the finest level.
layer_explain_wahlbezirke_ah16_short: Polling district boundaries, House of Representatives election 2016
layer_explain_wahlbezirke_ah16_long: Geometry of Berlin's polling districts for the Berlin House of Representatives (Abgeordnetenhaus) election 2016. Basis for spatially assigning election results at the finest level.
layer_explain_wahlbezirke_ah21_short: Polling district boundaries, House of Representatives election 2021
layer_explain_wahlbezirke_ah21_long: Geometry of Berlin's polling districts for the Berlin House of Representatives (Abgeordnetenhaus) election 2021. Basis for spatially assigning election results at the finest level.
layer_explain_wahlbezirke_ah23_long: Geometry of Berlin's polling districts for the 2023 repeat election of the Berlin House of Representatives (Abgeordnetenhaus). Basis for spatially assigning election results at the finest level.
layer_explain_wahlbezirke_bt25_long: Geometry of Berlin's polling districts for the Bundestag election 2025. Basis for spatially assigning election results at the finest level.
layer_explain_wahlbezirke_ah26_short: Polling district boundaries, House of Representatives election 2026
layer_explain_wahlbezirke_ah26_long: Geometry of Berlin's polling districts for the Berlin House of Representatives (Abgeordnetenhaus) and District Assembly (BVV) elections 2026. Basis for spatially assigning election results at the finest level.
layer_explain_wahlgruppen_btw17_long: Combined areas of polling districts and their shared postal district for the Bundestag election 2017. Smallest map level of the election results map.
layer_explain_wahlgruppen_ah16_short: Postal district groups, House of Representatives and District Assembly (BVV) elections 2016
layer_explain_wahlgruppen_ah16_long: Combined areas of polling districts and their shared postal district for the Berlin House of Representatives (Abgeordnetenhaus) and District Assembly (BVV) elections 2016. Smallest map level of the election results map.
layer_explain_wahlgruppen_ah21_short: Postal district groups, Bundestag, House of Representatives and District Assembly (BVV) elections 2021
layer_explain_wahlgruppen_ah21_long: Combined areas of polling districts and their shared postal district for the Bundestag election 2021, the Berlin House of Representatives (Abgeordnetenhaus) and District Assembly (BVV) elections 2021 and their 2023 repeat election. Smallest map level of the election results map.
layer_explain_wahlgruppen_bt25_long: Combined areas of polling districts and their shared postal district for the Bundestag election 2025. Smallest map level of the election results map.
layer_explain_wahlgruppen_ah26_short: Postal district groups, House of Representatives and District Assembly (BVV) elections 2026
layer_explain_wahlgruppen_ah26_long: Combined areas of polling districts and their shared postal district for the Berlin House of Representatives (Abgeordnetenhaus) and District Assembly (BVV) elections 2026. Smallest map level of the election results map.

disclaimer_historic: Historical record. Geometry from OpenStreetMap community data.
disclaimer_seasonal: Layer active May–October. November–April out of season.
disclaimer_source: Personal background taken from the cited source. Not generated algorithmically.
disclaimer_kuehle_orte: Geometry from OpenStreetMap (ODbL), supplemented with editorial enrichment. An offer, not a replacement for public authorities, and no legal entitlement to access.
disclaimer_compare_stolperstein: Stolpersteine commemorate victims of National Socialism. They are not a criterion for rating where to live. We only count them, without comparing or judging.
disclaimer_compare_mietspiegel: The rent index residential area class is not a measure of housing quality. A lower class does not mean “worse”.
disclaimer_compare_bodenrichtwerte: A higher standard land value can mean pricier rent, but often better amenities too. We show the difference without judging it.
disclaimer_compare_stigma_footer: Aggregated data per area reflect statistical averages, not individual living situations.
disclaimer_mss_aggregat: Structural aggregate data per planning area (around 7,500 residents). They do not represent individual addresses or people. As of: SenStadt MSS 2025.
disclaimer_compare_mss_aggregat: We show the level without judging it. Low status does not mean “bad Kiez”. Data per planning area, not per address.
disclaimer_kiez_score_explainer: Environment & infrastructure score from five dimensions per planning area (Quiet & air, Green & heat, Mobility, Local amenities, Tenant protection). Only measures variables where it is clear which direction is better. Social structure and affordability are deliberately excluded.
disclaimer_kriminalitaet_aggregat: Frequency rate per Bezirksregion, not address-level. It measures recorded cases per registered resident, not personal risk. Places with many tourists or commuters appear overstated, and unreported crime remains uncaptured. Not a safety ranking, not part of the overall score.
disclaimer_cross_layer_template: Values from different layers shown side by side, with no causal link. Aggregate data per planning area, not per address.
disclaimer_brw_not_aggregatable: Cannot be meaningfully aggregated at this level. A median across the whole area would blur local differences, so we show no value here.
disclaimer_level_below_threshold: Too little data at this level for a reliable statement. We would rather show no value than a misleading one.

layer_methodology_bezirke_calculation: Polygons of Berlin’s 12 administrative Bezirke from the Berlin geoportal, simplified for the map (small areas are kept).
layer_methodology_ortsteile_calculation: Polygons of the 96 statistical localities (Ortsteile), historically often independent municipalities before their incorporation in 1920. Source: ODIS Berlin.
layer_methodology_plz_calculation: Postcode areas for Berlin. One postcode can intersect several localities, so it does not match political boundaries.
layer_methodology_bodenrichtwerte_calcul: Location values for undeveloped land, set annually by the Berlin Committee of Valuation Experts (Gutachterausschuss) and aggregated by block. Value per square metre, differentiated by type of use.
layer_methodology_bodenrichtwerte_covera: Undeveloped land is the only basis of comparison. Values for developed plots are derived indirectly.
Special locations (railway land, cemeteries, water) appear without a value.
layer_methodology_bodenrichtwerte_omissi: No rent and no sale price. Rent index values belong to the layer “Rent index: residential area 2024”.
No indication of speculation or market prices.
layer_methodology_wohnlagen_2024_calcula: Aggregated residential area classification from the Berlin rent index (Mietspiegel) 2024 per LOR planning area, derived from the IBB housing market report. Ordinal scale from simple to prime location.
layer_methodology_wohnlagen_2024_coverag: Only one value per planning area. Block-level micro-locations disappear.
Commercial and mixed-use areas may appear without a residential area entry.
layer_methodology_wohnlagen_2024_omissio: Only the official rent index calculator (Mietspiegel-Rechner) at mietspiegel.berlin.de gives concrete €/m².
No statement on housing quality in the sense of “living better or worse”.
layer_methodology_milieuschutz_erhaltung: Polygons of the social preservation orders under §172 BauGB. Protection against displacement through modernisation and conversion.
Protection against rent increases can reduce the chances of moving. The layer does not assess this.
layer_methodology_milieuschutz_staedteba: Polygons of the urban preservation orders under §172 BauGB protecting the townscape (often old-building or Gründerzeit neighbourhoods).
layer_methodology_mss_gesamtindex_2025_c: Monitoring Social Urban Development 2025: overall index from two axes per LOR planning area. The status index (very low to high) weights income, employment and education. The dynamics index (negative, stable, positive) shows the change compared with the previous MSS cycle. Calculated by the Senate Department for Urban Development Berlin.
Planning areas with fewer than 300 residents or an outlier profile remain unclassified.
Aggregate data for around 7,500 residents each. Micro-locations disappear in the average.
layer_methodology_mss_gesamtindex_2025_o: Individual indicators such as the unemployment rate or the rate of welfare receipt are deliberately not shown in the address view. At address level they would be sharper and more stigmatising than the aggregate.
No rating as a “good” or “bad” Kiez. Low status reflects structural differences in income, employment and education, not housing quality.
layer_methodology_laerm_2023_calculation: Total traffic noise from road, rail and air traffic (LDEN), population-weighted per LOR planning area, from the Berlin Environmental Atlas (Umweltatlas) 2023. Three categories by quartile: low, medium, high.
layer_methodology_laerm_2023_coverage_ga: Model values, no city-wide network of monitoring stations.
Indoor noise in flats is not taken into account.
layer_methodology_laerm_2023_omission_0: No breakdown by source (road, rail, air traffic) at this aggregate level.
layer_methodology_laerm_2023_omission_1: Night-time noise indicators are separate in the Environmental Atlas, this layer shows overall pollution only.
layer_methodology_luft_2023_calculation: Modelled nitrogen oxide and particulate matter pollution per LOR planning area from the Berlin Environmental Atlas (Umweltatlas) 2023. Traffic model plus monitoring stations.
layer_methodology_luft_2023_coverage_gap: Aggregate per planning area, individual hotspots are averaged out.
layer_methodology_luft_2023_omission_0: Pollen and allergen exposure are not included.
layer_methodology_bioklima_2023_calculat: Bioclimatic summer stress per LOR planning area from the Environmental Atlas 2023. An indicator of urban heat island effects and soil sealing.
layer_methodology_bioklima_2023_coverage: Aggregate per planning area, the microclimate in courtyards is invisible.
layer_methodology_gruenversorgung_2023_c: Per-capita provision of public green and open space per LOR planning area from the Environmental Atlas 2023. Three categories: low, medium, high.
layer_methodology_gruenversorgung_2023_o: Private gardens and courtyards do not count towards per-capita provision.
layer_methodology_umweltgerechtigkeit_20: Combined index of noise, air, bioclimate and green space provision, weighted with social status. Identifies multiple burdens per LOR planning area.
Pre-aggregate of four individual layers. Avoid double counting in cross-layer indices.
No assessment of individuals, only a neighbourhood-level aggregate.
layer_methodology_klima_pet_2022_calcula: Physiological Equivalent Temperature (PET) on a hot day at 2 pm from the Berlin Climate Analysis 2022. Modelled on a 10 × 10 metre grid, reduced to polygon geometry here.
layer_methodology_klima_pet_2022_coverag: Not all urban areas are modelled. If an address lies up to 50 m from a modelled area, for example at a block edge, we show that area’s value.
layer_methodology_klima_kaltlufteinwirkb: Urban areas that benefit at night from cold air from forests, meadows and parks. Source: Berlin Climate Analysis 2022.
layer_methodology_klima_leitbahnkorridor: Valley structures, street corridors and open spaces through which cold air flows into the city at night.
Buildings in the corridors slow down the cooling. The layer shows geometry only, no calculation of losses.
layer_methodology_stolpersteine_calculat: Locations of the brass plaques for victims of National Socialism, laid in front of their last freely chosen homes. Concept by Gunter Demnig, data from OpenStreetMap, curated by local initiatives.
layer_methodology_stolpersteine_coverage: Coverage in OSM is incomplete. Not every set of stones laid has been mapped.
layer_methodology_stolpersteine_omission: Personal biographies come from external primary sources (stolpersteine-berlin.de). We do not generate any texts.
No housing score, no rating, no density statistics. The victims’ dignity outweighs comparability.
layer_methodology_kitas_2024_calculation: Recognised Berlin daycare facilities 2024 as a point layer. Run by public, church or independent providers.
layer_methodology_kitas_2024_omission_0: No occupancy rates or waiting list data.
layer_methodology_schulen_2024_calculati: General education schools from the Berlin school directory 2024 as a point layer.
layer_methodology_schulen_2024_omission_: No rating of school quality. Inspection reports are available separately from the Senate Department.
layer_methodology_einschulbereiche_2024_: Spatially defined primary school catchment areas. As a rule, children are assigned to the school of the catchment area they live in.
annually (at the change of school year)
Exceptions are possible, the layer shows only the standard assignment.
layer_methodology_krankenhaeuser_plan_ca: Hospitals in the Berlin hospital plan (Krankenhausplan) with a statutory care mandate.
layer_methodology_krankenhaeuser_weitere: Private or specialised hospitals outside the hospital plan, often rehabilitation or private clinics.
layer_methodology_sportanlagen_2024_calc: Sports venues from the Bezirk register of sports facilities 2024: sports grounds, halls, tennis facilities, swimming pools.
layer_methodology_gruenanlagen_calculati: Officially designated public green and recreational spaces, maintained by the Bezirk parks departments (Grünflächenämter).
layer_methodology_spielplaetze_calculati: Publicly accessible children’s playgrounds from the Berlin green spaces register (Grünanlagen-Register).
layer_methodology_spielplaetze_omission_: No inventory of play equipment, no data on refurbishment status.
layer_methodology_schwimmbaeder_calculat: Locations of Berliner Bäder-Betriebe and comparable facilities: indoor pools, outdoor summer pools, combined pools, lakeside bathing beaches.
layer_methodology_schwimmbaeder_omission: Seasonal opening hours and admission prices are not included.
layer_methodology_trinkbrunnen_calculati: Locations of public drinking fountains operated by Berliner Wasserbetriebe, derived from OpenStreetMap.
layer_methodology_trinkbrunnen_coverage_: Layer active May to October. Switched off outside the season for frost protection.
layer_methodology_kuehle_orte_calculatio: Places to cool down in the heat from OpenStreetMap, with editorial enrichment. The cool score from 1 to 5 follows type and construction (5 ice rink, 4 air-conditioned or by the water, 3 cool solid building). Of 659 places researched, the 519 suitable ones are included in the layer.
layer_methodology_kuehle_orte_coverage_g: Air conditioning can rarely be verified: 29 of 659 places have a verified AC status, the rest are likely or unknown. The AC note is an indication, not a guarantee.
layer_methodology_kuehle_orte_omission_0: Not a replacement for public authorities, no legal entitlement to access. Private places such as malls and cinemas exercise their right to refuse entry (Hausrecht).
layer_methodology_radverkehrsnetz_2025_c: Berlin cycling network including cycling priority routes 2025 under the Berlin Mobility Act (Mobilitätsgesetz). Line layer, derived from official geodata.
layer_methodology_fahrradstrassen_2024_c: Streets with sign 244.1 of the StVO, German road traffic regulations (bicycle street). Other vehicles only by exception and at walking pace.
layer_methodology_ubahn_stationen_calcul: BVG U-Bahn stations from OpenStreetMap route relations, filtered by operator BVG.
layer_methodology_sbahn_stationen_calcul: S-Bahn stations and halts from OpenStreetMap.
layer_methodology_tram_haltestellen_calc: BVG tram stops from OpenStreetMap, mainly in the eastern part of the city.
layer_methodology_bus_haltestellen_calcu: BVG bus stops for city and regional buses from OpenStreetMap.
layer_methodology_ubahn_netz_calculation: BVG U-Bahn line routes, 9 lines, from OpenStreetMap route relations, filtered by operator BVG.
layer_methodology_tram_netz_calculation: BVG tram line routes, 22 lines, from OpenStreetMap.
layer_methodology_sbahn_netz_calculation: Routes of the Berlin S-Bahn network, 16 lines, from OpenStreetMap route relations, filtered by operator S-Bahn Berlin GmbH.
layer_methodology_kiez_score_ruhe_luft_c: Weighted aggregation of noise and air per planning area (noise 0.5, air 0.5). Noise is a dB average (L_DEN) from the facade points of the 2022 strategic noise map: ≤45 dB → 100, ≥75 dB → 0, linear. Air as a 3-level index (low to high). Both normalised to 0–100, centroid-accurate per LOR polygon. Since the score reorganisation, bioclimate counts under Green & heat.
layer_methodology_kiez_score_ruhe_luft_u: every 3 to 5 years (in sync with Environmental Atlas updates)
layer_methodology_kiez_score_ruhe_luft_c: Noise dB is the average across the facade points in the LOR; quiet back courtyards without a facade point are not included.
Model values, no monitoring stations. Micro-locations of individual addresses remain invisible.
layer_methodology_kiez_score_ruhe_luft_o: Indoor exposure in flats not included.
No separate rating by source (road, rail, air traffic).
layer_methodology_kiez_score_gruen_hitze: Usable green space and heat protection per planning area: green space provision 0.30, proximity to green spaces 0.15, bioclimate 0.20, PET heat stress 0.15, cold air influence zone 0.10, cold air flow corridor 0.10. PET counts inversely (cooler = more points). Normalised to 0–100.
Private gardens and courtyards do not count towards public green space provision.
PET varies strongly at block level and is smoothed out in the LOR aggregate.
Quality and state of maintenance of parks not included.
layer_methodology_kiez_score_mobilitaet_: Distance-based, from the address point to the nearest U-Bahn (0.35), S-Bahn (0.25), tram (0.20) and bus (0.10) stop, plus Berlin-wide cycling network presence (0.10). 0 m equals 100, 1,000 m equals 0, linearly interpolated.
Service frequency and range of lines at the stop not taken into account.
Sharing services (bike, scooter, car) not included.
Quality of walking routes beyond straight-line distance not represented.
layer_methodology_kiez_score_versorgung_: Daycare measured twice: distance to the nearest daycare centre (weight 0.12, threshold 500 m) plus places per child aged 0–6 in the planning area (0.12). The per-capita term sums the registered daycare places in the LOR and divides them by the children aged 0–6 from the resident dataset: full points from 0.35 places per child, linear below that. Accessibility counts the number of facilities within the radius (density), not just the nearest one: more daycare centres/schools/playgrounds nearby score higher, a single location lower. Schools split by type: primary school (0.12, radius 600 m) and secondary school (0.12, 1,200 m). Plus playground density (0.10, 400 m) and local shops from OpenStreetMap (ODbL): groceries (0.12, 500 m: supermarket, discounter, Späti, bakery), pharmacy (0.07, 800 m) and post/parcel point (0.05, 1,000 m). If there is no facility within the radius, a soft transition based on the distance to the nearest one applies instead of a hard cut-off. Hospital in the Berlin hospital plan (0.18, 2,000 m) additionally weighted by bed capacity: a large general hospital counts more than a small specialist clinic. 0 m → 100, threshold → 0, linear. Playgrounds (polygons) use the geometric centre as the POI point. Since the score reorganisation, green spaces count under Green & heat. Local amenities therefore cover public services and private everyday local shops; the internal weights are provisional.
annually (in sync with education and Bezirk data)
The places-per-child ratio is based on registered capacity, not on actual occupancy rates or waiting lists.
Occupancy rates, waiting lists and type of provider are not taken into account in the score.
Polygon layers collapse to their centre. A long, narrow park on the edge appears centred in the score.
Local shops (groceries, pharmacy, post) are based on OpenStreetMap (crowdsourcing): individual locations may be missing or out of date.
No quality rating of the facility (the layer shows the location only).
Private hospitals and rehabilitation clinics are left out (hospitals in the Berlin hospital plan only).
layer_methodology_kiez_score_wohnschutz_: Protection against displacement per planning area: if the area lies in a Milieuschutz area (residential preservation statute or urban preservation statute, combined with OR), protection counts as in place (100), otherwise 0. At Bezirksregion/Bezirk level, the area-weighted share of protected planning areas. Unambiguously positive: more protection is better.
Protection status says nothing about actual rent trends in the area.
Area boundaries change with new orders, the data may lag behind.
Conversion ban, right of first refusal and approval practice of individual Bezirke not represented.
No statement on actual rent levels or displacement pressure.
layer_methodology_kiez_score_kultur_calc: Cultural access per planning area: log-damped density of collective cultural POIs nearby (number of facilities, the first place counts strongly, further ones level off). Library (weight 0.20, 1,000 m), theatre (0.15, 1,500 m), museum (0.15, 1,500 m), cinema (0.12, 1,500 m), community culture centre (0.13, 1,200 m), gallery (0.10, 1,200 m), public art (0.08, 800 m), club (0.07, 1,200 m). Source OpenStreetMap (ODbL). A separate dimension, NOT part of the overall score: culture clusters in the city centre, so it does not drive the headline score. Log damping prevents outer Bezirke from dropping to zero across the board.
layer_methodology_kiez_score_kultur_cove: Cultural venues from OpenStreetMap (crowdsourcing): individual locations may be missing or out of date.
The gap between inner city and outskirts is real: cultural infrastructure is concentrated in the city centre.
layer_methodology_kiez_score_kultur_omis: No rating of programme, quality or admission price of the venue.
Stolpersteine and monuments do NOT count (memorial/heritage, not a cultural amenity).
layer_methodology_kiez_score_kriminalita: Recorded crime per Bezirksregion: frequency rate (cases per 100,000 residents) of selected housing-relevant offences, equally weighted (0.20 each): neighbourhood offences (Kieztaten), residential burglary, vandalism, street robbery/bag snatching, bicycle theft. For each offence the 3-year average (2023–2025), from which the weighted index is derived, normalised to 0–100 (300 → 0, from 1,750 → 100). The upper limit caps city-centre outliers (government quarter, Alexanderplatz) whose frequency rate is overstated by tourists and commuters. The values are only available per Bezirksregion and are mirrored onto the planning areas it contains (constant within the Bezirksregion). A separate dimension, NOT part of the overall score, structural context like the social situation. Higher means more recorded cases, not a safety ranking.
Granularity Bezirksregion (143), coarser than the five dimensions native to planning areas.
The frequency rate relates cases only to registered residents, not to tourists, commuters or customers: inner-city hotspots appear overstated.
Unreported crime: only reported cases, and reporting behaviour varies by location.
Crime scene principle: only cases with an exact crime scene, pickpocketing excluded.
No statement on personal risk and no rating as a “safer” or “more dangerous” Kiez.
methodik_meta_description: Methodology of the Berlin data atlas: resolution, timeliness, editorial rules and what is deliberately not included.
methodik_mission_p1: navigator.berlin collects {layerCount} public Berlin geodata sets and shows the values that apply to each address. Served statically, without cookies, without login, without trackers.
methodik_mission_p2: The idea: make data readable without condensing it into a “residential score”. Neighbourhood statistics stay neighbourhood statistics. What applies at an address appears in the inspector. Where something does not apply, we say so.
methodik_architecture_p1: In the build step we fetch every layer from its source, reproject to EPSG:4326, simplify the geometry with mapshaper and write the hash plus the data update date into the manifest. At runtime a point-in-polygon lookup returns the applicable values per address. No database, no API call to the server.
methodik_aggregation_p1: Not every value is address-exact. Noise and air come from neighbourhood-level statistics (LOR planning area, 542 polygons). Standard land values attach to the city block. Anyone who reads a noise value in the inspector sees the mean for the whole planning area, not their own bedroom.
methodik_aggregation_level_address_detai: Point geocode + point layers (Stolpersteine, daycare centres, public transport stops)
methodik_aggregation_level_lor_detail: Noise, air, bioclimate, green space provision, environmental justice, residential areas 2024
methodik_aggregation_level_block_detail: Standard land values, climate PET, Milieuschutz, school catchment areas
methodik_aggregation_level_osm_detail: Cycling network, bicycle streets, public transport stations, Stolpersteine, drinking fountains
methodik_map_p1: The map shows at most two value maps at the same time, with fixed roles: the first fills the area, the second appears as graduated square symbols, one square per planning area, whose size shows the level. A third value layer automatically replaces the oldest. In the legend you can swap the roles with a click; the setting is carried over into shared links.
methodik_map_p2: Each score dimension has its own colour (Quiet & air blue, Mobility violet, Local amenities ochre, Tenant protection teal, Culture berry; green belongs to the overall score and Green & heat). Within each colour: light = low level, dark = high level. The shape language separates meanings: squares stand for aggregated area values, round markers and pins for specific places. Area layers such as Milieuschutz or cold air corridors only say “this applies here”, sit underneath as areas and do not count towards the two-map limit.
methodik_map_p3: The size gradation of the symbols carries the information even with red-green colour vision deficiency, where hues can converge. We measured the distinguishability of the colour combinations with simulated colour vision deficiency, not estimated it.
methodik_kiez_p1: In everyday speech a Kiez is a felt neighbourhood, defined by its residents, without a fixed boundary. On navigator.berlin, “Kiez” instead means an official unit: the LOR Bezirksregion (lifeworld-oriented spaces, LOR-BZR, as of 2021), 143 in total.
methodik_kiez_p2: We use the LOR Bezirksregion because only it has a clear, statistically backed boundary that all data hangs on. Your felt Kiez can be smaller or span several Bezirksregionen. The values on a Kiez page apply to the LOR-BZR, not to a single street.
methodik_cross_layer_p1: The environment & infrastructure score combines five dimensions per planning area: Quiet & air, Green & heat, Mobility, Local amenities (daycare centres, schools, hospitals, playgrounds) and Tenant protection (Milieuschutz areas). Each dimension stays separately available in the inspector and as its own map layer. Five times 20 percent weight. An overall layer aggregates them as a mean.
methodik_cross_layer_p2: The score only measures quantities with an unambiguous better direction for residents. It does not rate social structure: a Kiez with low social status does not live “worse”. Affordability also stays out: contested and without reliable address-level data.
methodik_cross_layer_p3: There is no single “Berlin score”. Aggregation to one number would stigmatise and obscure individual priorities. Someone looking for a place for a family weights differently from someone sensitive to heat.
methodik_mss_p1: The Monitoring Soziale Stadtentwicklung (social urban development monitoring) of the Senate Department for Urban Development, Building and Housing provides an overall index per planning area, made up of status (income, employment, education) and dynamics (change). Since the score reorganisation it no longer feeds into the score. We show it as a neutral context layer, only the aggregate value, not the individual indicators such as unemployment rate or rate of welfare receipt. Individual values would be sharper and more stigmatising at address level.
methodik_mss_p2: Low status does not mean “bad Kiez”. The level reflects structural differences, not housing quality. Choropleth colours are kept neutral, no red-green. Source: SenStadt MSS 2025, licence dl-de/zero-2-0.
methodik_election_p1: Bundestag, Berlin House of Representatives (Abgeordnetenhaus) and District Assembly (BVV) elections since 2011 with aggregates at four levels: polling district, Kiez (LOR Bezirksregion), Bezirk and Berlin overall. Sources are the Federal Election Commissioner (Bundeswahlleiterin, BTW) and the Statistics Office Berlin-Brandenburg (Amt für Statistik Berlin-Brandenburg, AGH + BVV). Values describe vote shares, not an assessment.
methodik_election_p2: We document special cases transparently: postal-vote groups as the smallest map level (Kiez value as an estimate), repeat elections 2023 with a reference to the original election, coverage gaps before 2017 without polling district geometry.
methodik_cool_places_p1: The Cool places layer shows places to cool down during heat. The cool score from 1 to 5 follows type and construction: 5 very cold (ice rink), 4 air-conditioned or by the water, 3 cool solid building such as a library or museum, below that less cool. Geometry and base tags come from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0, attribution), supplemented by an editorial navigator.berlin enrichment: cool score, air conditioning and summer availability.
methodik_cool_places_p2: Air conditioning is rarely verifiable: only 29 of 659 places have a verified AC status, the rest are marked probable or unknown. The AC note is an indication, not a promise. An offer, not a substitute for authorities, no legal right of access.
methodik_coverage_p1: If a layer delivers no value for an address, we state the reason.
methodik_coverage_reason_no_coverage: Dataset not available for this address.
methodik_coverage_reason_seasonal: Layer active only in season (drinking fountains May to October).
methodik_coverage_reason_out_of_concept: Layer conceptually not applicable (rent index layer in a commercial location).
methodik_omission_cookies_reason: No browser identification. Bookmarks live in LocalStorage.
methodik_omission_rent_reason: We state no €/m². The official value comes from mietspiegel.berlin.de.
methodik_omission_personal_data_reason: No profile, no behavioural analysis, no login requirement.
methodik_omission_generated_texts_reason: We write layer descriptions by hand. No LLM output for personal biographies.
methodik_omission_single_score_reason: There is one overall value per Kiez, but no single number for the whole of Berlin. Personal priorities weight things differently anyway.
methodik_editorial_p1: We show Stolpersteine as memorial markers. We neither count nor rate them. Personal biographies belong to the primary source stolpersteine-berlin.de.
methodik_editorial_p2: navigator.berlin states no rent price and gives no legal advice. The statutory rent index by residential area (Wohnlagen-Mietspiegel) comes from mietspiegel.berlin.de.
methodik_editorial_p3: Aggregated values are neighbourhood means, not properties of a flat. We deliberately forgo a “Berlin score” and show no Bezirk rankings.
methodik_editorial_p4: We write layer texts by hand. No layer content is summarised by LLM, no personal biography generated.
methodik_data_status_intro: Sorted alphabetically by layer name, not a ranking by recency.
methodik_licences_p1: Most layers are under dl-de/zero-2-0 or dl-de/by-2-0. OSM-based layers (Stolpersteine, public transport, drinking fountains, cycling) are under ODbL 1.0 with attribution to OpenStreetMap contributors.
methodik_feedback_p1: Methodology correction, data error or layer suggestion: by email.
methodik_daten_tabelle_caption: Data status table of all active layers
methodik_pipeline_figcaption: Build pipeline: all steps deterministic, idempotent, documented in the source repo.
methodik_kiez_score_meta_title: Methodology of the environment & infrastructure score - Berlin in data - navigator.berlin
methodik_kiez_score_meta_description: Kiez score methodology: seven dimensions (five in the overall score, culture and crime separate), normalisation, weights. Why social structure is not factored in. Berlin data atlas.
methodik_kiez_score_speakable_name: Methodology of the environment & infrastructure score
methodik_kiez_score_lead: Five dimensions per planning area, equally weighted, transparently traceable. The score measures environment and infrastructure, not social status.
methodik_kiez_score_worum_p1: The environment & infrastructure score is not a “Berlin ranking”. The map shows seven dimensions separately per planning area; the inspector aggregates them for a specific address. Five dimensions make up the overall score; culture and recorded crime sit alongside as standalone context dimensions. What applies is shown there. We also say what is missing or deliberately left out.
methodik_kiez_score_worum_p2: The planning area aggregation level corresponds to roughly 7,500 residents. Micro-locations of individual flats lie below that and do not appear in the aggregate.
methodik_kiez_score_dim_ruhe_luft_detail: Noise and air pollution, each weighted by half. Categorical 3-level mapping from low to high. Bioclimate no longer counts here; it has moved to Green & heat.
methodik_kiez_score_dim_gruen_hitze_laye: Green space provision 2023, Green spaces, Thermal stress 2023, Perceived temperature 2022, Cold air influence zone (2022), Cold air flow corridor (2022)
methodik_kiez_score_dim_gruen_hitze_deta: Usable green space and protection from heat. Green space provision 0.30, proximity to green spaces 0.15, bioclimate 0.20, PET heat stress 0.15, cold air influence zone 0.10, cold air flow corridor 0.10. PET counts inverted: cooler values give more points.
methodik_kiez_score_dim_mobilitaet_layer: U-Bahn, S-Bahn, tram and bus stops · Cycling network, Bicycle streets
methodik_kiez_score_dim_mobilitaet_detai: Straight-line distance from the address point to the nearest stop, with a detour factor of 1.3. U-Bahn 0.35, S-Bahn 0.25, tram 0.20, bus 0.10, cycling network presence 0.10. At 0 m one hundred points, at 1,000 m zero. Mobility uses the exact address distance, other dimensions the planning area centroid.
methodik_kiez_score_dim_versorgung_layer: Daycare centres, Schools, Hospitals in the Berlin hospital plan, Playgrounds, Groceries, Pharmacy, Post office
methodik_kiez_score_dim_versorgung_detai: Local amenities cover public services and private everyday local supply, each as density within a radius (number of facilities, soft transition instead of a hard distance cliff). Daycare accessibility (0.12) plus places per child (0.12), school by type (primary 0.12, secondary 0.12), hospital in the Berlin hospital plan weighted by capacity (0.18), playground (0.10). Plus local supply from OpenStreetMap (ODbL): groceries (0.12), pharmacy (0.07), post office (0.05). Green spaces count under Green & heat. Occupancy rate, ownership type and care quality are left out.
methodik_kiez_score_dim_wohnschutz_layer: Milieuschutz: rent preservation, Milieuschutz: urban planning
methodik_kiez_score_dim_wohnschutz_detai: Protection against displacement: if a planning area lies within a Milieuschutz area, protection counts as present. Residential preservation statute or urban planning preservation statute, combined with OR. This quantity is unambiguously positive: more protection is better for residents. Protection status says nothing about actual rent development.
methodik_kiez_score_dim_kultur_label: Culture (standalone, not in the overall score)
methodik_kiez_score_dim_kultur_layers: Museums, Galleries, Theatres & stages, Libraries, Cinemas, Community culture centres, Public art, Clubs
methodik_kiez_score_dim_kultur_detail: Cultural access as a log-dampened density of libraries, theatres, museums, cinemas, galleries, community culture centres, public art and clubs within a radius (OpenStreetMap, ODbL). The first cultural venue counts strongly, further ones flatten off, which dampens the inner-outer gradient. Culture is a separate, visible dimension but does NOT feed into the overall score: cultural infrastructure clusters in the inner city and would otherwise pull down the overall score of every outer Bezirk. Memorial sites (Stolpersteine, monuments) deliberately do not count.
methodik_kiez_score_dim_kriminalitaet_la: Recorded crime (standalone, not in the overall score)
Kiez score · recorded crime (Kriminalitätsatlas Berlin crime atlas, Berlin Police, dl-de-by-2.0)
methodik_kiez_score_dim_kriminalitaet_de: Frequency rate of selected housing-relevant offences (neighbourhood offences/Kieztaten, residential burglary, vandalism, street robbery, bicycle theft), equally weighted, as a 3-year mean 2023–2025. “Kieztaten” is a collective category of the Berlin Police for offences closely tied to the residential area (including bodily harm, threats, robbery, vandalism of motor vehicles, cellar and residential burglary). The values exist only per Bezirksregion (coarser than the five planning area dimensions) and are mirrored onto the planning areas they contain. City-core places with tourist and commuter distortion (government quarter, Alexanderplatz) are capped. A standalone context dimension in neutral indigo, NOT in the overall score and NOT a safety ranking. The frequency rate measures recorded cases per resident, not personal risk: the place-of-offence principle (Tatortprinzip), unreported crime and the resident denominator distort it. No “safe” or “dangerous”.
methodik_kiez_score_weights_p1: The “general” persona weights the five composite dimensions equally (20 percent each). Culture and recorded crime are visible context dimensions but do not count towards the overall score (weight 0). A persona switcher for family, single or senior users is in phase 2. Custom slider weighting also comes later.
methodik_kiez_score_norm_p1: Each raw value is translated to a 0-to-100 scale. Higher means more favourable.
methodik_kiez_score_norm_ordinal4_def: low 0, medium 33, high 66, very high 100 (local amenities)
methodik_kiez_score_norm_pet_def: 29 °C or cooler 100, 41 °C or hotter 0, linear in between
methodik_kiez_score_norm_p2: The 0-to-100 values within a dimension become a weighted mean using the layer weights. The dimension value is mapped to four UI levels: low (0–25), medium (26–50), high (51–75), very high (76–100).
methodik_kiez_score_kiez_score_p1: The 542 planning area values are aggregated to 143 LOR Bezirksregionen, weighted by area. A weighted mean is formed per dimension, with each planning area weighted by its area. At least 50 percent of the contained planning areas must have a value, otherwise the dimension stays without an aggregate.
methodik_kiez_score_kiez_score_p2: The composite score of a Bezirksregion is the unweighted mean of the non-null values of its five dimensions, in parallel with the address logic.
methodik_kiez_score_kiez_score_p3: LOR hierarchy: the first six characters of a planning area ID give the Bezirksregion ID, the first two the Bezirk code. Property-based mapping without a geometry test. If two Bezirksregionen share the same name, the Bezirk slug is appended as a suffix (e.g. heerstrasse-spandau, heerstrasse-charlottenburg-wilmersdorf).
methodik_kiez_score_bezirk_score_p1: At Bezirk level the 542 planning areas are aggregated directly, weighted by area, not via the Bezirksregion intermediate level. This keeps the weight of each planning area proportional to its actual area and independent of the LOR intermediate grouping.
methodik_kiez_score_bezirk_score_p2: Since the score reorganisation, all composite dimensions are unambiguously positive. That is why we also show an overall choropleth on the map (layer “Kiez score · overall”, high = better), in addition to the individual dimensions. Culture and recorded crime are standalone context dimensions and do not feed into the overall score. Crime and the MSS aggregate stay neutral context layers in neutral indigo, without red-green jumps. A city-wide “Berlin score” does not exist.
methodik_kiez_score_bezirk_score_pipelin: Build pipeline: {code_start}pnpm data:aggregate-scores{code_end} reads the planning area source, builds the LOR hierarchy and writes the aggregates idempotently into the Postgres tables {code_start}bezirk_score{code_end} and {code_start}kiez_score{code_end}.
methodik_kiez_score_missing_social_reaso: The social status of a Kiez is not a quality criterion. If we rated it, Kieze with low status would score worse and be stigmatised. The MSS aggregate stays visible as neutral context but does not feed into the score.
methodik_kiez_score_missing_affordabilit: Contested and ambivalent. High standard land values or highly rated residential areas mean expensive rent, not poor housing quality. Reliable address-level data is missing. Rent index values come from mietspiegel.berlin.de.
methodik_kiez_score_missing_family_reaso: Depends strongly on the persona: parents with a daycare child, a school-age child or care needs weight things differently. Daycare, school and hospital layers stay separate in the inspector instead of disappearing into a composite dimension.
methodik_kiez_score_sources_p1: Berlin Environmental Atlas (Umweltatlas; Senate Department for Urban Mobility, Transport, Climate Action and the Environment), Monitoring Soziale Stadtentwicklung (Senate Department for Urban Development Berlin), Berlin crime atlas (Kriminalitätsatlas Berlin; Berlin Police, dl-de-by-2.0) and public transport locations from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0). Full list with licence and data date per layer: {link_start}licences page{link_end}.
methodik_kiez_score_editorial_p1: The score is a statistical description of location, not an assessment of a flat. We state no rent price and give no legal advice.
methodik_kiez_score_editorial_p2: The score does not rate social structure. A Kiez with low social status does not live “worse”. We show the MSS aggregate as neutral context, not as an assessment. Choropleth colours for it stay neutral, without red-green jumps. Individual addresses can deviate strongly from the planning area mean.

methodik_wahldaten_meta_description: Election data methodology: sources, data cutoff, postal voting, polling district to Kiez aggregation and repeat elections in the Berlin data atlas.
methodik_wahldaten_intro_p1: This page documents the data sources, aggregation strategy and known coverage gaps of the election data. Values describe vote shares, not an assessment.
methodik_wahldaten_quellen_btw_desc: Federal Election Commissioner (Bundeswahlleiterin) polling district statistics ({code_start}_wbz.zip{code_end}). Obtained directly for each election year from {link_start}bundeswahlleiterin.de{link_end}. Licence: Data licence Germany, attribution, version 2.0.
methodik_wahldaten_quellen_agh_term: House of Representatives (Abgeordnetenhaus, AGH) + District Assembly (BVV)
methodik_wahldaten_quellen_agh_desc: Statistics Office Berlin-Brandenburg (Amt für Statistik Berlin-Brandenburg), XLSX sheet pipeline ({code_start}DL_BE_*.xlsx{code_end}). Obtained from {link1_start}statistik-berlin-brandenburg.de{link1_end}. Licence: Data licence Germany, attribution, version 2.0. AGH and BVV 2026 come directly from {link2_start}wahlen-berlin.de{link2_end} (Berlin State Election Commissioner, Landeswahlleiterin Berlin), as of the provisional official result.
methodik_wahldaten_quellen_geometrien_de: Statistics Office Berlin-Brandenburg, shapefile releases per election: {code_start}RBS_OD_Wahlgebiete_BTW17.zip{code_end}, {code_start}RBS_OD_UWB_AH21.zip{code_end}, {code_start}RBS_OD_UWB_AH26.zip{code_end} (polling district geometry AGH/BVV 2026) and others. Reprojection from ETRS89 UTM33 to WGS84 via mapshaper pipeline, simplify visvalingam + keep-shapes.
methodik_wahldaten_cutoff_p1: The election data cover elections from 2011. Pre-2011 data from the Federal Election Commissioner are partly available in different formats and require mapping to the 2001 Bezirk reform. Bundestag elections begin in 2013 because the Federal Election Commissioner publishes polling district data only from that year.
methodik_wahldaten_briefwahl_p1: Berlin counts postal votes in separate postal districts that have no area of their own, apart from the in-person polling districts. Bezirk and Berlin overall always include all votes because they sum over all polling districts.
methodik_wahldaten_briefwahl_p2: On the map, the postal-vote group is therefore the smallest level: all in-person polling districts of a postal district plus that postal district together form one area (dissolve of the in-person polygons), analogous to the Tagesspiegel presentation “Stimmbezirke 726, 727 und 7P”. This applies to all elections with polling district geometry.
methodik_wahldaten_briefwahl_p3: In the Kiez aggregate, postal voting is a proportional estimate by eligible voters, see {link1_start}section 4{link1_end}. For elections without polling district geometry, the map shows only Bezirk and Berlin level, see {link2_start}section 6{link2_end}.
methodik_wahldaten_aggregation_p1: Polling district values are aggregated spatially at four levels: polling district, Kiez (LOR Bezirksregion), Bezirk (12) and Berlin overall.
methodik_wahldaten_aggregation_p2: For the Kiez level, the polygon centroid is calculated for each polling district (via turf-center) and mapped to the LOR Bezirksregion that contains it (booleanPointInPolygon). Polling districts outside all LOR polygons stay unmapped and flow only into Bezirk + Berlin. The SQL aggregation sums per Kiez and party from the raw polling district rows (see scripts/build-wahl-kiez-aggregat.ts).
methodik_wahldaten_aggregation_p3: Postal votes flow in proportionally: each polling station of a postal-vote group receives a share of the group's postal votes ({code_start}ist_briefwahl_aggregat = true{code_end}) according to its eligible voters. This is an estimate, not an official split. If the eligible voters are missing for one or more polling stations of a group, the postal votes are distributed evenly across the group's polling stations.
methodik_wahldaten_wiederholung_p1: The Berlin Constitutional Court declared AGH 2021 + BVV 2021 partly invalid. AGH 2023 and BVV 2023 are the respective repeat elections. In the database they carry the flag {code_start}is_repeat_election{code_end} and refer to the respective original election via {code_start}parent_election_id{code_end}.
methodik_wahldaten_wiederholung_p2: The polling district geometry of the repeat election is identical to the original election of September 2021. The separate SBB source {code_start}RBS_OD_Wahllokale_AH23.zip{code_end} contains only polling station locations (points), not polling district polygons. That is why navigator.berlin maps AGH 2023 and BVV 2023 to the polygon layer {code_start}ah21{code_end} for the choropleth + Kiez aggregation.
methodik_wahldaten_geometrien_p1: Polling district polygons are available for: Bundestag 2017, 2021, 2025 as well as AGH + BVV 2016, 2021 (also used for the 2023 repeat election) and 2026. Bundestag 2013 as well as AGH + BVV 2011 have no published polling district geometries. These elections are accessible only at Bezirk and Berlin aggregate level. The Kiez aggregate is empty for them, and the choropleth component falls back to 12 Bezirk polygons with an inline note.
methodik_wahldaten_geometrien_p2: Reprojection: ETRS89 UTM33 → WGS84 via mapshaper Node API, simplify visvalingam + {code_start}keep-shapes{code_end} so that sliver polygons survive the simplify step.
methodik_wahldaten_cadence_p1: Election data are updated manually after each election. There is no live refresh from the source APIs, because the official final results only become available weeks after election day, and the Federal Election Commissioner and the Berlin State Election Commissioner do not publish their datasets through a stable API.
methodik_wahldaten_cadence_p2: AGH and BVV 2026 show the provisional official result from election day, 20 September 2026. The data is as of 21 September 2026. The source is wahlen-berlin.de (Berlin State Election Commissioner). The portal, election detail pages and API/tool responses mark the figures as “provisional” and show an as-of date where available. The final result is expected from 30 September 2026 (BVV) and from 5 to 8 October 2026 (AGH). When the final result arrives, a new data import replaces the provisional figures. The label then disappears.
methodik_wahldaten_cadence_p3: The build pipeline downloads and parses the raw data, rebuilds the polling district layers and updates the Kiez aggregate. A lint gate blocks evaluative vocabulary in code and docs.
methodik_wahldaten_alias_p1: Party names vary over the years (PDS → Die Linke, GRÜNE in spelling variants). A case-insensitive alias table in {code_start}scripts/wahlen/lib/partei-seed.ts{code_end} resolves source columns to canonical {code_start}kurzname{code_end} values. Unresolved entries end up under “Other” and are not listed in the inspector's top N.
methodik_wahldaten_cross_layer_p1: Election data appear on Kiez pages (see election trend block) and in the address inspector next to other layers (rent index residential area, noise mapping, rent index social level, Kiez score), without causal linking or evaluative framing. Editorial guidelines for this are in the {link_start}cross-layer templates preview{link_end} (noindex, co-design stage).

webmcp_meta_title: WebMCP - Interface for AI assistants - navigator.berlin
webmcp_meta_description: navigator.berlin WebMCP tools: delivering Berlin data to LLM agents. Spec status, browser support, tool calls.
webmcp_intro_p1: WebMCP is a browser API that lets websites deliver structured tools to AI agents. Instead of scraping HTML, the agent queries an address or a dataset directly and gets the number, source and licence back. navigator.berlin has delivered such tools since May 2026, now eleven of them. Since August 2026 one of them also writes: an agent can operate the Kiez Finder that a person sees in front of them.
webmcp_spec_p1: WebMCP is a {link_start}W3C Community Group draft{link_end}, developed jointly by Microsoft and Google and hosted in the Web Machine Learning Community Group. It is updated continuously, status as of August 2026. The API surface has since moved from {code_start}navigator.modelContext{code_end} to {code_start}document.modelContext{code_end}. It is explicitly not on the W3C standards track. That means interested parties have agreed on a draft, but there is no commitment yet to turn it into an official web platform API.
webmcp_support_chrome_desc: Origin trial from version 149, native implementation on {code_start}document.modelContext{code_end}. Can be enabled locally via the flag {code_start}chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing{code_end} plus a restart. As of September 2026.
webmcp_support_chatgpt_desc: The built-in browser provides {code_start}document.modelContext{code_end} natively. Tool calls require a runtime model with site tools support (GPT-5.6 Sol or Terra) and approval under Settings → Browser → Permissions.
webmcp_support_edge_desc: Origin trial from version 150. As of September 2026.
webmcp_support_firefox_desc: Mozilla lists WebMCP in its standards positions as “neutral”, with no worded position and no release date. As of September 2026.
webmcp_support_polyfill_desc: For browsers without a native implementation, LLM browser extensions often load a polyfill that supplies the API. navigator.berlin checks {code_start}document.modelContext{code_end} first and falls back to {code_start}navigator.modelContext{code_end} plus polyfill. This way the tools also work in Chrome Stable, Firefox or Safari, provided the agent takes this route.
webmcp_rationale_lead: The spec is a draft and browser support is new. We ship WebMCP tools anyway, because:
webmcp_rationale_li_discovery: Structured tool discovery is the right direction. HTML scraping by LLMs produces poor answers and unnecessary traffic. A declarative interface with source and licence per answer is an honest way to publish data.
webmcp_rationale_li_standards: Standards emerge when sites join early. A civic data platform should support such open web initiatives, not only commercial ones.
webmcp_rationale_li_effort: The effort is small. The tools are wrappers around functions that already exist (address lookup, layer query, election data). Spec changes affect only one adapter file.
webmcp_rationale_li_risk: If the spec breaks, one subpage fails. The main site stays usable. That limits the risk.
webmcp_tools_p1: Currently eleven tools are registered, ten reading and one writing. Full-text manifest with JSON schemas per tool at {link_start}/webmcp-manifest.json{link_end}.
webmcp_tool_address_lookup_desc: Search Berlin addresses, streets and POIs.
webmcp_tool_cross_layer_query_desc: Query all data layers at a coordinate, with the source for each value.
webmcp_tool_list_layers_at_point_desc: Which layers cover the point? A lean pre-check.
webmcp_tool_get_kiez_profile_desc: Profile of a LOR Bezirksregion: name, Bezirk, residents, area.
webmcp_tool_get_layer_metadata_desc: Source, licence, as-of date and methodology of a data layer.
webmcp_tool_get_election_result_desc: Result at an address for a given election, at a selectable level (polling district, Kiez, Bezirk, Berlin).
webmcp_tool_compare_elections_desc: Compare several elections at the same place, sparkline-ready.
webmcp_tool_get_voting_district_geometry: Return the GeoJSON polygon for a polling district ID.
webmcp_tool_set_finder_weights_desc: Writing: the agent sets the Kiez Finder sliders, and the map recolours live before the person's eyes.
webmcp_tool_get_finder_state_desc: Back channel: read the weights, the last source of change (person or agent) and the top Kieze.
webmcp_canary_step1: Install {link_start}Chrome Canary{link_end} version 149 or later (or Chrome Stable 149+).
webmcp_canary_step2: Open {code_start}chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing{code_end}, set “WebMCP for testing” to “Enabled” and restart Canary.

Plain-text variant for crawlers following {link3_start}llmstxt.org{link3_end}: {link4_start}/llms.txt{link4_end} and {link5_start}/llms-full.txt{link5_end}.

uis_meta_title: Environment & infrastructure score - Berlin in data - navigator.berlin
uis_meta_description: Environment & infrastructure score for Berlin: 143 Kieze and 12 Bezirke in five dimensions. Measures environment and infrastructure, not social status.
uis_intro_p1: Berlin Kieze and Bezirke sorted by five equally weighted dimensions. The score measures the environment and infrastructure of a Kiez, not social status. It bundles public data per planning area. A single address can differ from it.
uis_disclaimer: The score summarises public Senate data per LOR Bezirksregion. What feels good depends on personal priorities. A comparison, not a verdict.
uis_accordion_content: We aggregate five dimensions: quiet & air, green & heat, mobility, local amenities, tenant protection. The source for each dimension is open Senate data (noise mapping, green space supply, climate atlas, public transport stops, Milieuschutz areas, POI distances). Aggregation runs from 542 LOR planning areas → 143 LOR Bezirksregionen → 12 Bezirke, each weighted by area. Each dimension carries equal weight (5 × 20%). Social structure is deliberately not scored. {link_start}Full methodology · Kiez score{link_end}.
uis_empty_state: Score data will be released with the next build.
uis_ranking_crime_note: Recorded crime is a neutral context value (frequency rate per Bezirksregion, higher = more recorded cases), not a measure of quality. Deliberately not sortable and not part of the overall score: no safety ranking. Limits are described under {link_start}Methodology{link_end}.
webmcp_support_safari_desc: WebKit rejects WebMCP (“position: oppose”, June 2026). As of September 2026.
